questions.question: To build a basic solution of an equality-form LP, some variables are set to zero and the equations are solved uniquely for the others. Which variables are the basic variables?
options: Those whose values are solved from the equations
Those that are set to zero before solving begins
Those that are original decision variables only
Those that come out strictly positive at the end

questions.question: An equality-form LP has $m$ independent equations in $n$ variables ($n>m$). How many basic variables does each basic solution have?
options: $n-m$, one per zero variable
$m$, one for each equation
$n$, one for each variable
$1$, one per basic solution

questions.question: In a basic solution of an equality-form LP, variable $v$ is basic. What does this tell us about the value of $v$?
options: Only that the equations fix its value: it might be negative
That it is strictly positive, since zero values are excluded
That it is nonnegative, since basic means within the region
That it equals the right-hand side of one of the equations

questions.question: An LP with $\le$ constraints is written in equality form with decision variables $x_j$ and slacks $s_i$. Which variables can be basic in some basic solution?
options: Decision variables only, since slacks are always set to zero
Slacks only, because every $x_j$ is fixed at zero first
Any of them, slack or decision variable, by the choice made
Only variables that appear in every one of the equations

questions.question: In an equality-form LP with $m$ independent equations, what determines a basic solution, provided the equations can be solved uniquely?
options: The choice of exactly which $m$ variables are basic
The choice of the objective function to optimize
The choice of which $m$ variables are positive
The order in which the $m$ equations are written down

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$ (finishing, carpentry, soldier demand), with all variables required to be $\ge0$. With $s_1=s_2=0$, which variables are basic?
options: $x_s$, $x_t$ and $s_3$
$s_1$ and $s_2$ only
$x_s$ and $x_t$ only

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$ (finishing, carpentry, soldier demand), with all variables required to be $\ge0$. With $s_1=s_2=0$ and $x_s,x_t,s_3$ basic, what are their values?
The equality form $x_1+2x_2+s_1=8$, $3x_1+x_2+s_2=9$ (all variables required to be $\ge0$) has 4 variables and 2 equations. With $x_1=x_2=0$, which variables are basic and with which values?
Consider $x_1+2x_2+s_1=8$ and $3x_1+x_2+s_2=9$, where every variable is required to be $\ge0$. Fixing $x_1=s_2=0$ and solving, what values do the basic variables take?

Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$ (finishing, carpentry, soldier demand), with all variables required to be $\ge0$. In the basic solution with $s_1=s_2=0$, the basic variable $s_3$ equals $20$. What does this mean?
options: 20 finishing hours are left over in this production plan
20 soldiers too many are made for the demand limit
The soldier demand limit is binding in this plan
20 more soldiers could be sold before the demand limit

questions.question: In a basic solution of an equality-form LP, the variables that are not basic are set to zero. Which statement must then be true?
options: Every basic variable has a positive value
Each variable with a nonzero value is basic
Every slack variable in the LP is basic
Every decision variable in the LP is basic

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$ (finishing, carpentry, soldier demand), with all variables required to be $\ge0$. At $x_s=x_t=0$, $s_1$ is basic with value 100; at $s_1=s_2=0$ it is set to zero. What does this show?
options: $s_1$ is basic only when the plan is not optimal
Slacks switch to basic when their value exceeds 0
Being basic depends on the chosen basic solution
One of the two classifications must be an error

questions.question: An LP has constraints $\sum_ja_{ij}x_j\le b_i$, each with its own slack $s_i$ (coefficient 1 in equation $i$ only). Why are the slacks immediately solvable as basic variables when all $x_j=0$?
options: Slacks never appear in the objective, so they are free
Slacks are always nonnegative, so no solving is needed
The $x_j$ are the only variables that may be set to zero
Equation $i$ then reads $s_i=b_i$, one slack per equation

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$ (finishing, carpentry, soldier demand), with all variables required to be $\ge0$. Setting $x_t=s_1=0$, which basic variable comes out negative?
Giapetto's constraints with slacks are finishing $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, carpentry $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$ and soldier demand $x_s+s_3=40$. Can $x_t$, $s_1$, $s_2$ be the basic variables, with $x_s=s_3=0$?
options: No: the demand equation would then read $0=40$
Yes, the three values solve to $80$, $20$, $0$
No, a slack and its decision variable clash
Yes, any three of the five variables will do

questions.question: The equality form $x_1+2x_2+s_1=8$, $3x_1+x_2+s_2=9$ (all variables required to be $\ge0$) has 4 variables and 2 equations. If $x_1$ and $x_2$ are the basic variables, what are their values?
An LP with $m$ constraints of type $\le$ gets $m$ slacks, and each basic solution has $m$ basic variables. Why $m$ basic variables?
options: There are $m$ slacks, and each slack makes one basic variable
The $m$ independent equations fix exactly $m$ unknowns
There are $m$ decision variables, one per constraint
Half of all the variables are basic, which here gives $m$

questions.question: An equality-form LP has $m$ independent equations in $n$ variables ($n>m$). What can be said about the number of nonzero values in any basic solution?
options: At least $m$, since every basic variable is nonzero
Exactly $n-m$, one for every variable set to zero
At most $m$, as only basic variables can be nonzero
Exactly $n$, since every variable has a value

questions.question: The equality form $x_1+2x_2+s_1=8$, $3x_1+x_2+s_2=9$ (all variables required to be $\ge0$) has 4 variables and 2 equations. Maximizing $x_1+5x_2$ over the basic solutions with all values $\ge0$ gives $(x_1,x_2,s_1,s_2)=(0,4,0,5)$. Which statement is correct?
options: $x_1$ and $x_2$ are basic, as decision variables always are
$s_1$ and $s_2$ are basic, as the slacks always come first
$x_2$ and $s_1$ are basic, as $s_1$ is the binding constraint
$x_1$ is not basic here; $x_2$ and $s_2$ are the basic ones

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$ (finishing, carpentry, soldier demand), with all variables required to be $\ge0$. The demand limit drops from 40 to 15, and again $s_1=s_2=0$ with $x_s,x_t,s_3$ basic. Which statement is correct?
options: $s_3$ stops being basic, because its value would be negative
$x_s=20$, $x_t=60$ stay, and $s_3=-5$ makes it infeasible
All three values change, giving $x_s=15$, $x_t=65$, $s_3=0$
$s_3=0$, since the lower demand limit is now binding
